name: Airlock Bay
narrativeOnEnter: Emergency lighting bathes everything in cold blue. The outer airlock is sealed — standard for a station on lockdown. A pressure warning blinks on the wall panel. Somewhere above, a hull alarm is cycling. You have oxygen. For now.

hotspots.label: Corridor A
hotspots.lockedMessage: Emergency seal is engaged. The inner airlock door won't open until the seal code is entered.

action.text:
MERIDIAN STATION ALPHA
Emergency Procedures — Airlock Bay

In the event of lockdown, the inner airlock seal engages automatically.
Override code: 7743

(Standard crew safety requirement — code must be posted at all emergency stations.)

Life support status board is in Corridor A.
Engineering is accessible from Corridor A, lower hatch.

STATION O2 MONITOR — HANDHELD
Current Reading: 19.2% (NOMINAL)
Station Life Support: OFFLINE

Warning: Without life support, O2 levels will drop below safe threshold in approximately 30 minutes.

Restore power to life support from Engineering Deck immediately.

EMERGENCY STATUS — MERIDIAN STATION ALPHA

[!] LIFE SUPPORT — OFFLINE
[!] REACTOR DECK — CRITICAL
[✓] HULL INTEGRITY — NOMINAL
[!] COMMS — PARTIAL
[!] NEURAL EXTRACTION ARRAY — BUFFER FULL (standby mode)

Station lockdown initiated: 03:14 GST
Crew status: UNKNOWN

All personnel: proceed to emergency muster stations.

───
You read it twice before it registers.

[!] NEURAL EXTRACTION ARRAY — BUFFER FULL (standby mode)

Neural Extraction Array.
On a space station.
In a section of the status board between hull integrity and comms,
as if it belongs there.

As if it's standard equipment.

The outer airlock is sealed and vacuum-locked. Standard procedure during station emergencies.

Through the small porthole: open space. Stars.

Two shapes.

The closer one — 800 metres, running full lights — is MERIDIAN-3. Standard rescue shuttle configuration. The registry markings are barely visible but legible: HELIOS GROUP, Registration No. HG-3301.

The farther one — 3 kilometres out, beyond visual without the porthole magnifier — is dark. Running no lights, no transponder. Smaller than MERIDIAN-3. Holding position precisely, as if it's watching.

You don't know what it is.
You don't know why it's running dark.
But it's been there since before you woke up.
And it hasn't moved.

Someone out there is watching to see how this ends.
